## Stages
<!-- The ordered phases. One subsection per stage; for each capture Id / Actions / Flows / Touchpoints /
     Mindset / Pain points / Opportunities / Evidence / Next as bold-label bullets — the one per-block
     bullet form the tree uses ([[_authoring:wiki-template-labels#template-labels]]). A dropped bullet
     is a `template-bullets` finding, so a stage with nothing to record writes `None.` after the
     label. The form of Id, Flows, Opportunities, Evidence and Next is in
     [[_authoring:wiki-journey-cell-grammars#journey-cell-grammars]].
     Id is a kebab id, unique on the page across stages and opportunities. Flows links the
     task-flow(s) realizing the stage via [[product:flows/<module>/<task>]], separated by `,`;
     `None.` means the product should carry the stage out but no flow does yet, and
     `Outside the product.` means the stage happens off-product — a buyer journey's stages mostly do.
     Touchpoints name channels, never a surface: surfaces cite the stages they serve in their own
     Journey stages bullet. Opportunities hold one sub-bullet each, naming a page `owner` value and the
     metric that shows it worked, or an open question in place of the metric (`Open question: <question>`);
     a stage with none writes `None.`. Evidence names the
     research the stage rests on, as `domain:` links separated by `;`; a claim no research backs is
     written `Assumption: <claim>` there and listed under Open questions, naming the stage's Id, with
     the research that would settle it. Next names the stage ids a branch leads to, separated by `,`;
     `None.` means the next stage in page order.
     The stage arc is drawn from these bullets: `/wiki-reindex` writes it to
     `_derived/graph-journeys.md`, so draw nothing by hand. A rendered export of the journey map goes in
     the `artifacts:` field.
     This page owns the phase arc: `gtm-plan` and `sales-playbook` link it for the buyer
